subject.title: fix: require decimal numeric oc-path predicates

question: Should relational oc-path predicates intentionally narrow their public numeric grammar from finite JavaScript-coercible numbers to plain decimal literals only?
rationale: The patch is mechanically small, but accepting or rejecting exponent and hexadecimal forms is a public CLI compatibility decision rather than a test-only repair.

options.title: Adopt strict decimal grammar
options.body: Confirm decimal-only relational operands as the supported contract, document the compatibility change, and retain tests for rejected legacy coercions.

options.title: Preserve finite-number compatibility
options.body: Keep the established finite-number predicate grammar and narrow the fix to the specific unsafe coercions that maintainers agree should be rejected.

recommendation.title: Adopt strict decimal grammar
recommendation.body: Confirm decimal-only relational operands as the supported contract, document the compatibility change, and retain tests for rejected legacy coercions.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline’s direct mention supplies the strongest available evidence of a person positioned to resolve this public behavior decision.
